task.title: Installing Unity and Connecting It to Visual Studio
task.shortdesc: Install Unity Hub, install the Unity Editor, and configure Visual Studio as your default script editor so you can write and debug C# scripts from within Unity.

ul.li: An active internet connection for the initial download

context.p: Unity Hub manages your Unity Editor versions and projects. You install Unity Hub first, then use it to install a specific Editor version.

step.cmd: Go to the Unity Personal page and select Get started or Download Unity.

image.alt: Unity Personal product page showing the Get started and Download Unity buttons.

step.cmd: Sign in with a Unity ID, or create a free one if you do not already have one.
step.info: A Unity ID is required to activate a license. Continue with Google, Apple, SSO, or email.

image.alt: Unity account creation screen with Continue with Google, Apple, SSO, and Email options.

step.cmd: Confirm your operating system and download Unity Hub.
step.info: Unity detects your OS automatically (Windows, in this example) and the download starts right away. If it does not start automatically, select your OS and architecture manually.

image.alt: Post-download onboarding page with Windows detected and Open, Install, Launch steps listed.

step.info: On Windows, this opens the Unity Hub Setup wizard. Confirm or browse to a destination folder, check that enough disk space is available, and select Install.

image.alt: Unity Hub Setup wizard showing the Choose Install Location screen.

step.cmd: In Unity Hub, select Installs > Install Editor.
step.info: Select the latest LTS (Long-Term Support) version unless your project specifies a different version.

step.cmd: In the module selection screen, enable Microsoft Visual Studio Community if it is not already installed, or enable Visual Studio Editor if Visual Studio is already present.
step.stepresult: The Unity Editor and the selected modules begin downloading.

step.cmd: Once installation completes, open Unity Hub and select New Project.
Choose a template, name the project, and select Create Project.
step.stepresult: Unity creates the project and opens the Editor.

step.cmd: In Unity, go to Edit > Preferences > External Tools and confirm the External Script Editor field is set to Visual Studio.
step.info: If it is not set automatically, select Visual Studio from the dropdown list.

step.cmd: Double-click any .cs script in the Project window to confirm it opens directly in Visual Studio with Unity's C# project references loaded.
step.stepresult: Visual Studio opens with IntelliSense recognizing Unity API classes such as MonoBehaviour, confirming the two applications are correctly linked.

result.p: Unity and Visual Studio are now installed and connected. You can write, save, and run C# scripts in Visual Studio and see the results reflected immediately in the Unity Editor.

postreq.p: See Running Your First Script to test the connection end-to-end.
